Thanks for the details — quick internal calc and recommended framing for procurement.

High level unit economics (baseline assumptions):
- Baseline (US hosted, optimized model, quantized FP16/INT8 as applicable): ~ $18–$24 per 1M tokens at 1–3k token/session profiles depending on batching.
- EU hosted (same model family, EU region infra): add ~15% hardware + networking uplift => $21–$28 per 1M tokens.
- Data residency (Private/VPC with customer-managed network & KMS): add fixed monthly premium (example: $6k/mo) + unit uplift of ~8–12% depending on the degree of isolation and storage encryption requirements.

Example scenarios (rounded):
- US hosted pilot: target pricing we can propose = $20 per 1M tokens (with recommended batching params and 1–2% discount for pilot commit).
- EU hosted (hosted region, no VPC): $24 per 1M tokens.
- EU Private/VPC: $24 base + 10% uplift => ~ $26.5 per 1M tokens + $6k/mo platform premium.

Notes / levers to hit their $20–$35 target:
- Aggressive quantization & batching can reduce unit cost by 10–25% but may impact latency/quality. Recommend evaluating on their prompt set.
- Commitment/volume discount tiers: for 1B+ tokens/month we can move pricing into low teens per 1M with a 12–24 month commit.
- Managed caching (prefix caching of common prompts) could reduce effective tokens by 15–30% for KYC flows with recurring prompts.

Next steps to close procurement ask by Tue:
- Marissa: confirm whether they prefer Hosted EU region + VPC vs Private full on-prem for the EU requirement.
- Dylan: can you pull the exact platform premium numbers for a VPC (monthly + typical unit uplift range) and an example contract clause for data residency?

I can draft the US vs EU two-column pricing and callout the platform premium.

— Sean
